passages.text: I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of God’s wrath.
passages.sermon:
I am a man.
I have seen affliction.
God showed His anger.
God used His rod against me.
passages.original: אֲנִ֤י הַגֶּ֙בֶר֙ רָאָ֣ה עֳנִ֔י בְּשֵׁ֖בֶט עֶבְרָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He has driven me away and made me walk in darkness instead of light.
passages.sermon:
God acted against me.
God drove me away.
God made me walk in darkness.
God did not let me walk in light.
passages.original: אוֹתִ֥י נָהַ֛ג וַיֹּלַ֖ךְ חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וְלֹא־ אֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Indeed, He keeps turning His hand against me all day long.
passages.sermon:
God is angry with me.
He acts against me.
He turns His hand against me.
He does this again and again.
He does this all day long.
passages.original: אַ֣ךְ בִּ֥י יָשֻׁ֛ב יַהֲפֹ֥ךְ יָד֖וֹ כָּל־ הַיּֽוֹם׃ס

passages.text: He has worn away my flesh and skin; He has shattered my bones.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power.
God has worn away my flesh.
God has worn away my skin.
God has shattered my bones.
passages.original: בִּלָּ֤ה בְשָׂרִי֙ וְעוֹרִ֔י שִׁבַּ֖ר עַצְמוֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: He has besieged me and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.
passages.sermon:
God acts against me.
God surrounds me.
God brings bitterness to me.
God brings hardship to me.
passages.original: בָּנָ֥ה עָלַ֛י וַיַּקַּ֖ף רֹ֥אשׁ וּתְלָאָֽה׃

passages.text: He has made me dwell in darkness like those dead for ages.
passages.sermon:
God has placed me in darkness.
I sit in this darkness.
I am like people who died long ago.
I remain in this place, far from light.
I feel cut off, as if I am among the dead.
passages.original: בְּמַחֲשַׁכִּ֥ים הוֹשִׁיבַ֖נִי כְּמֵתֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃ס

passages.text: He has walled me in so I cannot escape; He has weighed me down with chains.
passages.sermon: God has walled me in.\r\nI cannot escape.\r\nGod has weighed me down with chains.
passages.original: גָּדַ֧ר בַּעֲדִ֛י וְלֹ֥א אֵצֵ֖א הִכְבִּ֥יד נְחָשְׁתִּֽי׃

passages.text: Even when I cry out and plead for help, He shuts out my prayer.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is suffering.
The speaker cries out.
The speaker pleads for help.
God shuts out the speaker’s prayer.
passages.original: גַּ֣ם כִּ֤י אֶזְעַק֙ וַאֲשַׁוֵּ֔עַ שָׂתַ֖ם תְּפִלָּתִֽי׃

passages.text: He has barred my ways with cut stones; He has made my paths crooked.
passages.sermon:
God blocked my ways with large stones.
God made my paths twisted.
God prevented me from moving forward.
God changed my direction so I could not go straight.
passages.original: גָּדַ֤ר דְּרָכַי֙ בְּגָזִ֔ית נְתִיבֹתַ֖י עִוָּֽה׃ס

passages.text: He is a bear lying in wait, a lion hiding in ambush.
passages.sermon:
God acts against me.
He waits for me like a bear.
He hides like a lion ready to attack.
He prepares to harm me when I do not expect it.
passages.original: דֹּ֣ב אֹרֵ֥ב הוּא֙ לִ֔י אַרְיֵה בְּמִסְתָּרִֽים׃

passages.text: He forced me off my path and tore me to pieces; He left me without help.
passages.sermon:
God acted against me.
He forced me off my path.
He tore me to pieces.
He left me alone.
He left me without help.
passages.original: דְּרָכַ֥י סוֹרֵ֛ר וַֽיְפַשְּׁחֵ֖נִי שָׂמַ֥נִי שֹׁמֵֽם׃

passages.text: He bent His bow and set me as the target for His arrow.
passages.sermon: God is the subject.\r\nGod bent His bow.\r\nGod made me the target for His arrow.
passages.original: דָּרַ֤ךְ קַשְׁתוֹ֙ וַיַּצִּיבֵ֔נִי כַּמַּטָּרָ֖א לַחֵֽץ׃ס

passages.text: He pierced my kidneys with His arrows.
passages.sermon:
God is the subject.
God acts with power and judgment.
God sent His arrows into me.
His arrows pierced my kidneys.
passages.original: הֵבִיא֙ בְּכִלְיוֹתָ֔י בְּנֵ֖י אַשְׁפָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I am a laughingstock to all my people; they mock me in song all day long.
passages.sermon:
All my people laugh at me.
They treat me as a joke.
They sing songs to mock me.
They do this all day long.
passages.original: הָיִ֤יתִי שְּׂחֹק֙ לְכָל־ עַמִּ֔י נְגִינָתָ֖ם כָּל־ הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: He has filled me with bitterness; He has intoxicated me with wormwood.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power.
God fills me with bitterness.
God gives me wormwood to drink.
God makes me drunk with this bitterness.
passages.original: הִשְׂבִּיעַ֥נִי בַמְּרוֹרִ֖ים הִרְוַ֥נִי לַעֲנָֽה׃ס

passages.text: He has ground my teeth with gravel and trampled me in the dust.
passages.sermon: God caused me to suffer.\r\nHe pressed my teeth into gravel.\r\nHe pushed me down into the dust.
passages.original: וַיַּגְרֵ֤ס בֶּֽחָצָץ֙ שִׁנָּ֔י הִכְפִּישַׁ֖נִי בָּאֵֽפֶר׃

passages.text: My soul has been deprived of peace; I have forgotten what prosperity is.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is suffering deeply.
The speaker’s soul has no peace.
The speaker cannot remember good things.
The speaker has forgotten prosperity.
passages.original: וַתִּזְנַ֧ח מִשָּׁל֛וֹם נַפְשִׁ֖י נָשִׁ֥יתִי טוֹבָֽה׃

passages.text: So I say, “My strength has perished, along with my hope from the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
The speaker is suffering deeply.
The speaker feels weak.
The speaker says, "My strength is gone."
The speaker has lost hope.
The speaker says, "My hope from the LORD has perished."
passages.original: וָאֹמַר֙ אָבַ֣ד נִצְחִ֔י וְתוֹחַלְתִּ֖י מֵיְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Remember my affliction and wandering, the wormwood and the gall.
passages.sermon:
I am suffering.
I am wandering.
I experience bitterness.
I taste poison.
Remember my suffering.
Remember my wandering.
Remember my bitterness.
Remember my pain.
passages.original: זְכָר־ עָנְיִ֥י וּמְרוּדִ֖י לַעֲנָ֥ה וָרֹֽאשׁ׃

passages.text: Surely my soul remembers and is humbled within me.
passages.sermon: My soul remembers my suffering.\r\nMy soul feels humbled inside me.
passages.original: זָכ֣וֹר תִּזְכּ֔וֹר וְתָשִׁיחַ עָלַ֖י נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: Yet I call this to mind, and therefore I have hope: Because of the loving devotion of the LORD we are not consumed, for His mercies never fail.
passages.sermon:
I remember something important in my heart.
This gives me hope.
The LORD shows loving devotion.
Because of this, we are not destroyed.
His mercies never end.
His mercies never fail.
passages.original: זֹ֛את אָשִׁ֥יב אֶל־ לִבִּ֖י עַל־ כֵּ֥ן אוֹחִֽיל׃ס חַֽסְדֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ כִּ֣י לֹא־ תָ֔מְנוּ כִּ֥י לֹא־ כָל֖וּ רַחֲמָֽיו׃

passages.text: They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness!
passages.sermon: God’s mercies are new every morning.\r\nGod’s faithfulness is great.
passages.original: חֲדָשִׁים֙ לַבְּקָרִ֔ים רַבָּ֖ה אֱמוּנָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: “The LORD is my portion,” says my soul, “therefore I will hope in Him.”
passages.sermon:
My soul speaks.
My soul says, "The LORD is my portion."
The LORD belongs to me.
The LORD gives me what I need.
Because of this, I will hope in Him.
passages.original: חֶלְקִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אָמְרָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֔י עַל־ כֵּ֖ן אוֹחִ֥יל לֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: The LORD is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul who seeks Him.
passages.sermon: The LORD is good.\r\nHe is good to those who wait for Him.\r\nHe is good to every soul who seeks Him.
passages.original: ט֤וֹב יְהוָה֙ לְקוָֹ֔ו לְנֶ֖פֶשׁ תִּדְרְשֶֽׁנּוּ׃

passages.text: It is good to wait quietly for the salvation of the LORD.
passages.sermon: The LORD saves people.\r\nIt is good to wait for the LORD.\r\nWait quietly for the LORD’s salvation.
passages.original: ט֤וֹב וְיָחִיל֙ וְדוּמָ֔ם לִתְשׁוּעַ֖ת יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: It is good for a man to bear the yoke while he is still young.
passages.sermon: A man should bear the yoke when he is young.\r\nThis is good for him.
passages.original: ט֣וֹב לַגֶּ֔בֶר כִּֽי־ יִשָּׂ֥א עֹ֖ל בִּנְעוּרָֽיו׃ס

passages.text: Let him sit alone in silence, for God has disciplined him.
passages.sermon: God has disciplined this person.\r\nHe should sit alone.\r\nHe should remain silent.
passages.original: יֵשֵׁ֤ב בָּדָד֙ וְיִדֹּ֔ם כִּ֥י נָטַ֖ל עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Let him bury his face in the dust— perhaps there is still hope.
passages.sermon:
A man suffers because God has disciplined him.
He should put his face down into the dust.
He should stay low and humble.
There may still be hope for him.
passages.original: יִתֵּ֤ן בֶּֽעָפָר֙ פִּ֔יהוּ אוּלַ֖י יֵ֥שׁ תִּקְוָֽה׃

passages.text: Let him offer his cheek to the one who would strike him; let him be filled with reproach.
passages.sermon: A person suffers because God has disciplined him.\r\nHe should offer his cheek to the one who strikes him.\r\nHe should accept shame and reproach.
passages.original: יִתֵּ֧ן לְמַכֵּ֛הוּ לֶ֖חִי יִשְׂבַּ֥ע בְּחֶרְפָּֽה׃ס

passages.text: For the Lord will not cast us off forever.
passages.sermon: The Lord is our God.\r\nThe Lord will not reject us forever.\r\nThe Lord does not abandon His people for all time.
passages.original: כִּ֣י לֹ֥א יִזְנַ֛ח לְעוֹלָ֖ם אֲדֹנָֽי׃

passages.text: Even if He causes grief, He will show compassion according to His abundant loving devotion.
passages.sermon:
God sometimes causes grief.
God also shows compassion.
God has great loving devotion.
God’s compassion matches His abundant loving devotion.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אִם־ הוֹגָ֔ה וְרִחַ֖ם כְּרֹ֥ב חַסְדּוֹ׃

passages.text: For He does not willingly afflict or grieve the sons of men.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is compassionate.
He does not want to cause pain.
He does not choose to bring suffering to people.
He does not willingly afflict anyone.
He does not willingly grieve the sons of men.
passages.original: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א עִנָּה֙ מִלִּבּ֔וֹ וַיַּגֶּ֖ה בְנֵי־ אִֽישׁ׃ס

passages.text: To crush underfoot all the prisoners of the land, to deny a man justice before the Most High, to subvert a man in his lawsuit— of these the Lord does not approve.
passages.sermon:
The Lord does not approve of certain actions.
He does not approve when someone crushes all the prisoners of the land underfoot.
He does not approve when someone denies a man justice before the Most High.
He does not approve when someone subverts a man in his lawsuit.
The Lord rejects these actions.
passages.original: לְדַכֵּא֙ תַּ֣חַת רַגְלָ֔יו כֹּ֖ל אֲסִ֥ירֵי אָֽרֶץ׃ לְהַטּוֹת֙ מִשְׁפַּט־ גָּ֔בֶר נֶ֖גֶד פְּנֵ֥י עֶלְיֽוֹן׃ לְעַוֵּ֤ת אָדָם֙ בְּרִיב֔וֹ אֲדֹנָ֖י לֹ֥א רָאָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Who has spoken and it came to pass, unless the Lord has ordained it?
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the Most High.
He has supreme authority.
No one can make something happen unless the Lord commands it.
No person can speak and cause an event unless God has ordained it.
Only what God allows or commands will happen.
passages.original: מִ֣י זֶ֤ה אָמַר֙ וַתֶּ֔הִי אֲדֹנָ֖י לֹ֥א צִוָּֽה׃

passages.text: Do not both adversity and good come from the mouth of the Most High?
passages.sermon:
The Most High is God.
God speaks.
God sends both adversity and good.
Both hardship and blessing come from God.
Nothing happens unless God allows it.
passages.original: מִפִּ֤י עֶלְיוֹן֙ לֹ֣א תֵצֵ֔א הָרָע֖וֹת וְהַטּֽוֹב׃

passages.text: Why should any mortal man complain, in view of his sins?
passages.sermon: Every person is a sinner.\r\nEvery living man has sinned.\r\nNo man should complain about his life because of his sins.
passages.original: מַה־ יִּתְאוֹנֵן֙ אָדָ֣ם חָ֔י גֶּ֖בֶר עַל־ חֶטְאוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Let us examine and test our ways, and turn back to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
We are people who have sinned.
We must look closely at our actions.
We must test our ways.
We must turn back to the LORD.
passages.original: נַחְפְּשָׂ֤ה דְרָכֵ֙ינוּ֙ וְֽנַחְקֹ֔רָה וְנָשׁ֖וּבָה עַד־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Let us lift up our hearts and hands to God in heaven: “We have sinned and rebelled; You have not forgiven.”
passages.sermon:
God is in heaven.
God is holy.
Let us lift up our hearts to God.
Let us lift up our hands to God.
We have sinned.
We have rebelled against God.
God, You have not forgiven us.
passages.original: נִשָּׂ֤א לְבָבֵ֙נוּ֙ אֶל־ כַּפָּ֔יִם אֶל־ אֵ֖ל בַּשָּׁמָֽיִם׃ נַ֤חְנוּ פָשַׁ֙עְנוּ֙ וּמָרִ֔ינוּ אַתָּ֖ה לֹ֥א סָלָֽחְתָּ׃ס

passages.text: You have covered Yourself in anger and pursued us; You have killed without pity.
passages.sermon:
God is angry.
God hides Himself in His anger.
God chases us.
God kills us.
God does not show pity.
passages.original: סַכֹּ֤תָה בָאַף֙ וַֽתִּרְדְּפֵ֔נוּ הָרַ֖גְתָּ לֹ֥א חָמָֽלְתָּ׃

passages.text: You have covered Yourself with a cloud that no prayer can pass through.
passages.sermon:
God is the subject.
God has covered Himself.
God used a cloud to cover Himself.
No prayer can pass through this cloud.
passages.original: סַכּ֤וֹתָה בֶֽעָנָן֙ לָ֔ךְ מֵעֲב֖וֹר תְּפִלָּֽה׃

passages.text: You have made us scum and refuse among the nations.
passages.sermon:
God acts in anger.
God pursues us.
God kills without pity.
God covers Himself with a cloud.
No prayer can pass through this cloud.
God makes us scum among the nations.
God makes us refuse among the nations.
passages.original: סְחִ֧י וּמָא֛וֹס תְּשִׂימֵ֖נוּ בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָעַמִּֽים׃ס

passages.text: All our enemies open their mouths against us.
passages.sermon:
Our enemies surround us.
They speak against us.
Every enemy opens his mouth.
They accuse us.
They attack us with words.
passages.original: פָּצ֥וּ עָלֵ֛ינוּ פִּיהֶ֖ם כָּל־ אֹיְבֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Panic and pitfall have come upon us— devastation and destruction.
passages.sermon:
We are the people of Israel.
We feel panic.
We face pitfalls.
Devastation has come to us.
Destruction has come to us.
passages.original: פַּ֧חַד וָפַ֛חַת הָ֥יָה לָ֖נוּ הַשֵּׁ֥את וְהַשָּֽׁבֶר׃

passages.text: Streams of tears flow from my eyes over the destruction of the daughter of my people.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a person from Israel.
The speaker sees the destruction of the people of Israel.
The speaker feels deep sorrow.
Tears stream from the speaker’s eyes.
The speaker cries because the people of Israel have been destroyed.
passages.original: פַּלְגֵי־ מַ֙יִם֙ תֵּרַ֣ד עֵינִ֔י עַל־ שֶׁ֖בֶר בַּת־ עַמִּֽי׃ס

passages.text: My eyes overflow unceasingly, without relief, until the LORD looks down from heaven and sees.
passages.sermon:
My eyes overflow with tears.
My tears do not stop.
I find no relief.
This continues until the LORD looks down from heaven.
The LORD sees my suffering.
passages.original: עֵינִ֧י נִגְּרָ֛ה וְלֹ֥א תִדְמֶ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין הֲפֻגֽוֹת׃ עַד־ יַשְׁקִ֣יף וְיֵ֔רֶא יְהוָ֖ה מִשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

passages.text: My eyes bring grief to my soul because of all the daughters of my city.
passages.sermon:
I am the speaker.
I feel deep sorrow.
My eyes cause pain to my soul.
I grieve because of all the daughters of my city.
passages.original: עֵינִי֙ עֽוֹלְלָ֣ה לְנַפְשִׁ֔י מִכֹּ֖ל בְּנ֥וֹת עִירִֽי׃ס

passages.text: Without cause my enemies hunted me like a bird.
passages.sermon: My enemies hunted me.\r\nThey had no reason.\r\nThey hunted me like a bird.
passages.original: צ֥וֹד צָד֛וּנִי כַּצִּפּ֖וֹר אֹיְבַ֥י חִנָּֽם׃

passages.text: They dropped me alive into a pit and cast stones upon me.
passages.sermon: My enemies attacked me without cause.\r\nThey threw me alive into a pit.\r\nThey cast stones at me.
passages.original: צָֽמְת֤וּ בַבּוֹר֙ חַיָּ֔י וַיַּדּוּ־ אֶ֖בֶן בִּֽי׃

passages.text: The waters flowed over my head, and I thought I was going to die.
passages.sermon: Water covered my head.\r\nI believed I would die.
passages.original: צָֽפוּ־ מַ֥יִם עַל־ רֹאשִׁ֖י אָמַ֥רְתִּי נִגְזָֽרְתִּי׃ס

passages.text: I called on Your name, O LORD, out of the depths of the Pit.
passages.sermon:
I was in a deep pit.
I was alive when they threw me in.
They cast stones on me.
I felt trapped and hopeless.
I called on You, LORD.
I spoke Your name from the depths.
I cried out to You from the lowest place.
passages.original: קָרָ֤אתִי שִׁמְךָ֙ יְהוָ֔ה מִבּ֖וֹר תַּחְתִּיּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: You heard my plea: “Do not ignore my cry for relief.”
passages.sermon:
God, You heard my voice.
I asked for help.
I begged for relief.
I said, “Do not turn away from me.”
I said, “Listen to my cry.”
passages.original: קוֹלִ֖י שָׁמָ֑עְתָּ אַל־ תַּעְלֵ֧ם אָזְנְךָ֛ לְרַוְחָתִ֖י לְשַׁוְעָתִֽי׃

passages.text: You drew near when I called on You; You said, “Do not be afraid.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord is near to me.
I called to the Lord.
The Lord came close to me on the day I called.
The Lord spoke to me.
The Lord said, "Do not be afraid."
passages.original: קָרַ֙בְתָּ֙ בְּי֣וֹם אֶקְרָאֶ֔ךָּ אָמַ֖רְתָּ אַל־ תִּירָֽא׃ס

passages.text: You defend my cause, O Lord; You redeem my life.
passages.sermon:
O Lord, you defend my cause.
You fight for my soul.
You redeem my life.
You save me.
passages.original: רַ֧בְתָּ אֲדֹנָ֛י רִיבֵ֥י נַפְשִׁ֖י גָּאַ֥לְתָּ חַיָּֽי׃

passages.text: You have seen, O LORD, the wrong done to me; vindicate my cause!
passages.sermon:
The LORD sees everything.
The LORD sees the wrong done to me.
The LORD knows I have suffered injustice.
I ask the LORD to judge my case.
I ask the LORD to make things right for me.
passages.original: רָאִ֤יתָה יְהוָה֙ עַוָּ֣תָתִ֔י שָׁפְטָ֖ה מִשְׁפָּטִֽי׃

passages.text: You have seen all their malice, all their plots against me.
passages.sermon:
The Lord sees everything.
The Lord sees all the malice of my enemies.
The Lord sees every plan they make against me.
The Lord knows all their plots against me.
passages.original: רָאִ֙יתָה֙ כָּל־ נִקְמָתָ֔ם כָּל־ מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֖ם לִֽי׃ס

passages.text: O LORD, You have heard their insults, all their plots against me— the slander and murmuring of my assailants against me all day long.
passages.sermon:
O LORD, you have heard their insults.
You have heard all their plans against me.
My enemies speak slander against me.
They whisper and murmur about me all day long.
passages.original: שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ חֶרְפָּתָם֙ יְהוָ֔ה כָּל־ מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֖ם עָלָֽי׃ שִׂפְתֵ֤י קָמַי֙ וְהֶגְיוֹנָ֔ם עָלַ֖י כָּל־ הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: When they sit and when they rise, see how they mock me in song.
passages.sermon:
My enemies sit down.
My enemies stand up.
They do this often.
They mock me in their songs.
I see their mocking.
passages.original: שִׁבְתָּ֤ם וְקִֽימָתָם֙ הַבִּ֔יטָה אֲנִ֖י מַנְגִּינָתָֽם׃ס

passages.text: You will pay them back what they deserve, O LORD, according to the work of their hands.
passages.sermon:
The LORD sees what people do.
The LORD knows the actions of those who attack me.
The LORD will repay them.
He will give them what they deserve.
He will judge them by the work of their hands.
passages.original: תָּשִׁ֨יב לָהֶ֥ם גְּמ֛וּל יְהוָ֖ה כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Put a veil of anguish over their hearts; may Your curse be upon them!
passages.sermon:
God, you act with justice.
You can cover their hearts with anguish.
You can place a veil of pain over them.
You can send Your curse upon them.
passages.original: תִּתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ מְגִנַּת־ לֵ֔ב תַּאֲלָֽתְךָ֖ לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: You will pursue them in anger and exterminate them from under Your heavens, O LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is angry.
The LORD will pursue them.
The LORD will destroy them.
The LORD will remove them from under His heavens.
passages.original: תִּרְדֹּ֤ף בְּאַף֙ וְתַשְׁמִידֵ֔ם מִתַּ֖חַת שְׁמֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ
